## P04.1 execution observations

- Relative-path prepare returned run 3f7f99dd6992eb6ec8dc70ac8ebc94a5143decc2ee75041f6d10f22a6613a553, but later journal inspection found no durable item row. Absolute-path recovery persisted the same run identity; its actual timestamp is retained in the journal and prepare-recovery.json. No earlier start timestamp was reconstructed.
- The initial exact filtered Composer command sent the filter only to the isolated TasksWorkflow invocation, which reported no tests. Composer now forwards explicit filters to the primary suite and always runs TasksWorkflow.
- Required full lint originally found only the immutable P04-design inventory script. Its bytes remain digest-bound to the design input manifest; a single pinned artifact exclusion avoids rewriting admitted inputs.
- Initial source integration required adding seven Foundation zone records and reclaiming exactly two namespace declaration tokens from the old custom-fields rename inventory. Old class and child-namespace negatives remain red.
- Four schema worker timeout assertions occurred in the first broad SQLite run during concurrent host work. Isolated affected tests (7/65) and the serial full SQLite run (847 + 10) passed without product changes.
- Golden --update emits already-renamed historical records too. The approved-delta candidate retains the original baseline plus only seven new Attribute/tooling records; the other three layers remain exactly the original bytes.

- First package aggregate used host PG 5432 and hit tenancy Composer timeout=900s with preceding tests passing. Retry uses the package-declared Docker PG 5434 corex_test and COMPOSER_PROCESS_TIMEOUT=0, without changing repository timeouts or test assertions.
- Mutation command returned 0 but selected baseline probes revealed schema/setup errors under concurrent package execution. Final evidence requires serial baseline/mutant reruns after all package tests stop; the pg-lane-split case intentionally has zero selected baseline tests and must select failing PG tests only under its mutation.

## Final serial mutation evidence

All 33 ordinary original mutation commands pass without sabotage after package suites finish. The existing P1.14-pg-lane-split control deliberately selects zero tests with the PG lane excluded (exit 1 due to failOnEmptyTestSuite); under sabotage it selects five PG tests and fails on the intentionally invalid port. All 34 sabotaged commands fail for their boundary. The serial rerun removes the schema errors seen while package and root Testbench suites overlapped; concurrent runs are not used as acceptance evidence. Package aggregate passes on its configured isolated Docker port 5434 with only the process timeout disabled. See mutation-baselines.json, baseline-*.log, mutations.log and packages.log.

## Independent review and final bookkeeping

See review-findings.md and review-verdict.md. One bare PHPDoc collection finding was fixed with failing-then-passing controls and positive generic collection fixtures. The owner requested no extra audits; only the existing review concluded and confirmed its own fix. First CLI infrastructure attempt had no output and was terminated; final reviewer session provenance is retained. After the product commit, anti-weakening required the missing D64 REBASELINE row; it was added to the same local commit. No baseline or assertion threshold was weakened.
